Republic of the Philippines DEPARTMENT OF THE INTERIOR AND LOCAL GOVERNMENT A. Francisco Gold Condominium II Bldg, EDSA corner Mapagmahal St., Diliman, Quezon City OFFICE OF THE SECRETARY OPINION NO. 24 S. 2010 08 March 2010 MR. PIACIDO W. SEGUNDO Secretary to the Sanggunian Tubo, Abra Dear Mr.Segundo: This has reference to your earlier letter asking our legal advice/opinion on the following queries: (1) Is it required to employees under the Legislative Branch or Sangguniang Bayan Office of the Local Government Unit to follow or observe the regular office hours 8:00 AM — 12:00 Noon and 1:00 PM from Monday to Friday? I am asking this question because Sangguniang Bayan is among those 24 hours duty in government service, and because of this they may schedule their activities, meetings and even their regular session at any time appropriate for them, wherein employees are necessary to be in volved (e) Who will approved (sic) the Official Business Travel and Itinerary of Travel of employees under the Sangguniang Bayan Office? In reply to your first query, please be informed that neither the Local Government Code of 1991 (RA 7160) nor any regulation has fixed the office hours of elective officials. The rationale for this is understandable for it would violate the very nature of the work of elective officials who are considered on call anytime of the day. Fixing their working hours would unnecessarily delimit their sennces to the prejudice of their constituents and ultimately, the public service. With respect to appointed employees, including those in the local sanggunian, the Omnibus Rules implementing Book V of Executive Order No. 292 and other pertinent Civil Service Laws require _them to render only eight (8) hours of work a day. They are not required to attend sanggunian sessions, except the Secretary to the Sanggunian whose function is primarily to record the minutes of the session. This notwithstanding, the latter's attendance to the session conducted by the sanggunian is not a measure for the rendition of his work but rather his completion of eight (8) hours work a day per CSC rules. With regard to your second query, please be advised that the Mayor, as the Chief Executive of the Municipal Government, has the power to authorize official trips of municipal officials and employees outside of the municipality for a

period not exceeding thirty (30) days pursuant to Section 444 of the Local Government Code of 1991. We hope that we have addressed your concern accordingly. Very truly yours, By Authority of the Secretary: ATIY. J Direct copy furnished: Regional Director Patrick D. Onus DILG-CAR Barangay Center, Baguio City Ls/17:ins U B. DOQ EIV Ill Legal Se •ce
